Ukrainian authorities introduced a new air raid alert system on September 6. The change is an attempt to preserve normal life and the country’s economic health as Russian drone attacks become more frequent and destructive.





The mass production of jet drones has enabled Russia to bypass Ukrainian air defense systems to reach a range of economic and civilian targets that Ukraine had effectively shielded from older Shahed-type drone variants.



Ukraine is struggling to counter this new aerial threat. Until new countermeasures are developed, Ukrainian authorities face the difficult dilemma of saving lives, preserving societal functions, and protecting the economy all at once.

latest_rss.title: ‘Russian Citizens of Tajik Origin’ Pose New National Challenges for Moscow
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




A large new nationality is emerging in the Russian Federation, a more than 800,000-strong group now called “Russian citizens of Tajik origin,” which Moscow is struggling to manage and that challenges how the Russian government will deal with others.



Culturally and linguistically Tajik but legally Russian, Russian citizens of Tajik origin cannot easily be forced to leave, forced to assimilate, or blocked from forming ethnic enclaves except at the price of  Moscow’s relationship with Tajikistan and its base there.



Moscow is addressing these problems by promoting the political careers of some Russian citizens of Tajik origin. This approach may help in the short term but is likely to trigger larger problems in the future.

Drones and other unmanned platforms provide the JLSF units with an increased capacity to evacuate wounded personnel to field hospitals and other medical sites for treatment.



The use of intelligent equipment such as electronic casualty tags and telemedicine surgery capabilities enhances the JLSF’s ability to effectively treat wounded personnel.



The JLSF’s live-saving chain would likely face some limitations, such as developing an overreliance on unmanned platforms that can be jammed, and which emit substantial electromagnetic signatures that can assist targeting.

latest_rss.title: Russia and Pakistan Sign Deal on Rail Connectivity
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Pakistan and Russia signed a freight-forwarding contract on August 31 to establish a framework for international freight transportation and pursue a pilot container train linking Pakistan with Russia, Central Asia, and possibly Belarus.



Earlier efforts to launch the connection have been repeatedly delayed, including a planned June 2025 pilot that was cancelled amid conflict in Iran. Each proposed route would transit Iran, with options discussed through Central Asia or Azerbaijan.



The project faces significant infrastructure and security challenges, including Iran’s incomplete rail links, differing railway standards, and instability along proposed routes. If completed, it could expand Russia’s access to South Asia and Pakistani ports.
